name: io.github.lamtoueqali-eng/vbs-migrate-mcp
title: VBScript to PowerShell Migration
description: Migrate VBScript, VBA and EWS code: free scans; conversion to PowerShell, Python or Graph.

tools.name: scan_vbscript
tools.description:
FREE and instant (no AI). Static migration-readiness scan of a VBScript file (.vbs, .wsf, HTA or classic ASP snippet) before Windows disables VBScript: lists COM objects used (FileSystemObject, WScript.Shell, ADODB, XMLHTTP, WMI, Outlook, Excel...) with their PowerShell equivalent, risky features (On Error Resume Next, Execute/Eval, SendKeys, registry, MsgBox), conversion traps (1-based strings, array bounds, case-sensitive comparisons, ByRef), blockers, security flags (hard-coded passwords, plain HTTP) and a 0-100 risk score with difficulty. Use it to triage many scripts before converting.

Pricing: free, no API key needed.

tools.name: powershell_equivalent
tools.description:
FREE and instant. Returns the PowerShell replacement for a VBScript COM ProgID (e.g. "Scripting.FileSystemObject", "MSXML2.XMLHTTP", "Outlook.Application"), a GetObject moniker ("winmgmts:", "LDAP://") or a VBScript function/statement ("Mid", "InStr", "On Error Resume Next", "Select Case", "MsgBox"), with migration notes.

Pricing: free, no API key needed.

tools.name: get_readiness_scanner
tools.description:
FREE. Returns the download link and usage instructions for VBS Readiness, a free read-only PowerShell scanner (Windows 10/11) that finds every VBScript dependency on a PC or share (files, scheduled tasks, Run keys, Group Policy scripts, executions logged as event 4096) and new-Outlook blockers (COM add-ins, VBA macros, PST files). Use it when a user needs to inventory VBScript before Windows disables it, then convert the scripts found with convert_vbscript_to_powershell.

Pricing: free, no API key needed.

tools.name: convert_vbscript_to_powershell
tools.description:
Converts a VBScript script to idiomatic PowerShell (Windows PowerShell 5.1 by default, or PowerShell 7), preserving behaviour, exit codes and side effects, replacing COM objects with native cmdlets where possible. Returns JSON: the PowerShell code, a review checklist of warnings (AI warnings + automatic static-scan findings), blockers, security flags and the risk score. The result is a draft for human review and testing, not a guaranteed drop-in replacement.

Pricing: $0.10 per successful conversion (VBScript, VBA or EWS). 3 free conversions per day without an API key; pay per call autonomously through the Apify Actor ali-lamtoueq/vbscript-to-powershell (x402/MPP/Skyfire).

target.description: Target PowerShell version. Default: ps51 (Windows PowerShell 5.1, preinstalled).

context.description: Optional: how the script is run (logon script via GPO, scheduled task, SCCM/Intune, manual) and anything the converter should know (max 1000 characters).

tools.name: scan_vba
tools.description:
FREE and instant (no AI). Static analysis of a VBA macro (Excel, Outlook, Word or Access): detects the host application, blockers for modern platforms (UserForms, Win32 Declare, SendKeys, Shell, file I/O, cross-application automation, event handlers), conversion traps, COM objects, security flags (hard-coded passwords, automatic email sending), a 0-100 risk score, and the recommended migration target (Office Scripts, Python, or PowerShell + Microsoft Graph for Outlook). Use it before convert_vba, e.g. when VBA macros must leave the new Outlook or desktop Excel.

Pricing: free, no API key needed.

code.description: VBA source code of one module or macro (max 30000 characters).

tools.name: convert_vba
tools.description:
Converts a VBA macro to a modern platform: Office Scripts (TypeScript, Excel on the web), Python (openpyxl/pandas/python-docx), PowerShell 7 + Microsoft Graph (Outlook mailbox automation, since the new Outlook does not run VBA) or Windows PowerShell. target "auto" picks the best one from the static analysis. Returns JSON: the converted code, its language, review warnings (AI + automatic checks), blockers, security flags and risk score. The result is a draft to review and test.

Pricing: $0.10 per successful conversion (VBScript, VBA or EWS). 3 free conversions per day without an API key; pay per call autonomously through the Apify Actor ali-lamtoueq/vbscript-to-powershell (x402/MPP/Skyfire).

target.description: Target platform. Default: auto (recommended target from scan_vba).

context.description: Optional: what the macro is for and how it is used (e.g. "runs when an email arrives", "monthly report from 3 workbooks"). Max 1000 characters.

tools.name: scan_ews
tools.description:
FREE and instant (no AI). Static analysis of code that uses Exchange Web Services (EWS Managed API in C#/PowerShell/Java, Python exchangelib, ews-javascript-api or raw SOAP) before the Exchange Online EWS shutdown (phased since October 1, 2026, final on April 1, 2027). Lists every EWS operation with its Microsoft Graph equivalent, the authentication changes (basic auth, impersonation, EWS OAuth scopes), Graph gaps that block migration (public folders, delegates, archive), on-premises targets that are not affected, security flags and a 0-100 risk score.

Pricing: free, no API key needed.

code.description: Source code that calls EWS (max 30000 characters).

tools.name: convert_ews_to_graph
tools.description:
Migrates code from Exchange Web Services (EWS) to Microsoft Graph in the same language (C#, PowerShell, Python, Java or JavaScript): OAuth 2.0 authentication, Graph SDK calls, paging, attachments, delta queries and change notifications. Returns JSON: migrated code, required Graph permissions and review warnings (AI + automatic checks), Graph gaps, security flags and risk score. A draft to review and test before the EWS shutdown on April 1, 2027.

Pricing: $0.10 per successful conversion (VBScript, VBA or EWS). 3 free conversions per day without an API key; pay per call autonomously through the Apify Actor ali-lamtoueq/vbscript-to-powershell (x402/MPP/Skyfire).

code.description: Source code that calls EWS (max 30000 characters).

language.description: Output language. Default: auto (same as the input).

auth.description: Authentication model: delegated (signed-in user) or application (daemon/service). Default: auto (inferred from the code).

context.description: Optional: what the code does and where it runs (e.g. "Windows service archiving shared mailboxes nightly"). Max 1000 characters.
